rules.status: Useful if a dietary gap exists
rules.reason: Protein powder can help fill a known dietary protein gap. If food already meets your needs, adding powder is optional.
Creatine monohydrate has evidence for repeated high-intensity exercise and resistance-training adaptations. It is not required to begin training.
Low fish intake is a reason to review dietary omega-3 sources, not proof that a fish-oil supplement will prevent disease. Compare verified EPA+DHA.
Some short trials suggest benefits for stress or sleep with specific extracts. Long-term safety and equivalence across products remain uncertain.
A bone-health goal alone does not establish vitamin D deficiency or justify a high-strength product. Confirm the need and suitable formulation with a clinician.

rules.status: Not an automatic sleep or recovery add-on
rules.reason: Review dietary intake and an established reason for supplementation. A salt name or elemental amount does not establish a sleep benefit.
Assess calcium, magnesium and zinc separately. A combined tablet is not automatically better than addressing an individual dietary gap.
